analysis.one_liner: India's largest oil refiner and fuel retailer, running 10 refineries (about 31% of the country's refining capacity) and selling petrol, diesel, LPG and other fuels through a nationwide network, majority-owned by the Government of India.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results were declared on 30 October 2026: consolidated PAT jumped to ₹22,503 crore (standalone ₹21,630 crore, up roughly 184% year-on-year) on revenue up about 29-30% to roughly ₹2.6-2.7 lakh crore. The stock rallied about 5% on 2 November as crude prices pulled back and refining margins improved. A meaningful part of the profit jump was a one-off: the government recognised ₹7,243 crore of LPG under-recovery compensation for April-September 2026 within this quarter's numbers.
analysis.plain_terms: Indian Oil is a government-controlled company that buys crude, refines it, and sells fuel at prices Delhi partly controls - so its profit depends as much on crude costs and subsidy timing as on how much fuel it sells. The 184% profit jump sounds dramatic, but the year-ago quarter was weak and this quarter includes a one-time subsidy payment, so it overstates how much the underlying business actually improved. Just one quarter earlier, in Q1 FY27, the company posted an outright loss when crude prices spiked during the West Asia conflict and fuel prices at the pump weren't raised to match. The tension to hold onto: this looks statistically cheap, but a chunk of that cheapness is the market pricing in just how unpredictable quarter-to-quarter profit can be.
analysis.quarters: Consolidated trend (₹ crore - revenue/EBITDA/PAT): Q3 FY25 194,014/9,509/2,147; Q4 FY25 195,270/19,548/8,368; Q1 FY26 192,341/17,999/6,808; Q2 FY26 178,628/20,475/8,191; Q3 FY26 205,157/27,372/13,502; Q4 FY26 208,289/30,261/15,176; Q1 FY27 266,407/5,205/-1,141 (consolidated loss; standalone loss was reported closer to ₹2,661 crore - sources diverge on standalone vs consolidated here, flagging rather than averaging); Q2 FY27 ~253,967-268,039/38,227/22,503. Management attributed the Q1 FY27 loss to average crude costs rising to about $100.7/bbl from $83/bbl the prior quarter without matching retail price hikes, plus an inventory hit. The Q2 FY27 rebound combined a genuine margin recovery (reported GRM $10.66/bbl, normalised GRM $8.9/bbl, both up on quarter) with the ₹7,243 crore one-off LPG compensation booking - the two should not be read as the same thing.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock is up 99.84% versus the Nifty's 28.58% and peer BPCL's 67.42% - strong long-run outperformance. Over 3 years it's up 70.91% against the Nifty's 20.83%, though behind BPCL's 91.58%. More recently it has lagged: -16.19% over 1 year versus the Nifty's -10.92% (roughly in line with BPCL's -16.38%), and the stock sits 29.1% below its 27 Feb 2026 peak of ₹183.5, though still above its 52-week low of ₹125.35. The company has gone through six stock splits since 1996 (most recently 1.5-for-1 in June 2022) - these are splits, not spin-offs or demergers, so there's no shareholder value lost that needs adding back; the long-run return figures already reflect split-adjusted prices.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates across sources range from roughly 4x to 6.5x, among the cheapest in its sector (one source puts the sector median P/E near 8.7x). The stock trades close to or just below book value (P/B roughly 0.8-0.9x against a book value near ₹165/share). Why it's cheap: earnings are lumpy and partly government-controlled (subsidy timing, capped marketing margins, a quarter that can flip from loss to large profit), so the market is discounting for unpredictability rather than mispricing a stable business. Whether that discount is fair is a separate question this report can't answer - it depends on whether GRMs and subsidy flows normalise going forward.
analysis.growth_read: Revenue growth (Q2 FY27 up ~29.5% YoY) is mostly price and cost pass-through plus a weak year-ago base, not volume - domestic product sales volume grew a modest 4.9% YoY (23.977 MMT versus 22.851 MMT). So this quarter's growth is margin/price-led rather than volume-led, which per the company's own commodity-business dynamics is the less durable kind. A capacity expansion is underway - the Panipat refinery is being expanded from 15 to 25 MTPA at an approved cost of ₹38,231 crore, reportedly 90-95% complete and targeted for completion around December 2026 - which should eventually add genuine volume growth.
analysis.health_read: ROE is roughly 19-20.5% and ROCE about 18.7%, both healthy on paper for a capital-intensive PSU. But profits are not a steady translation of operations into cash quarter to quarter - they swing with crude prices, inventory valuation, and when the government chooses to recognise LPG subsidy compensation (as seen going from a loss in Q1 FY27 to a large profit in Q2 FY27). Borrowings stand around ₹1.3 lakh crore against a debt/equity ratio near 0.6x (moderate, not high), funding a large capex programme (₹32,700 crore planned for FY27, with ₹12,162 crore spent in H1). The dominant concern here is business risk from crude and subsidy volatility, not balance-sheet/solvency risk.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India, via the President of India, holds 51.5% - unchanged for five consecutive quarters - with fellow PSUs ONGC (14.2%) and Oil India (5.16%) also on the register. FIIs hold about 8.6%, DIIs about 10%, and retail investors about 10.4%. No promoter pledging was found in available sources; as a sovereign promoter, formal pledging is not typical, but this specific figure is Not verified - check on Screener. No marquee individual investor appears on the shareholding pattern.
strengths: India's largest refiner with 10 refineries and 80.75 MMTPA capacity (~31% of domestic refining capacity)
ROE of roughly 19-20.5% and ROCE of about 18.7%, solid returns for a capital-intensive PSU
TTM dividend yield of 6.34% (TTM dividend ₹8.25/share), attractive for income-focused holders
5-year share price return of 99.84% has far outpaced the Nifty's 28.58% over the same period
watchpoints: Earnings swung from a loss in Q1 FY27 (crude price spike, no matching retail price hike) to a ₹21,630-22,503 crore profit in Q2 FY27 - this is not a steady operating trend
Roughly ₹7,243 crore of the Q2 FY27 profit was a one-off government LPG subsidy recognition, not repeatable operating income
Stock remains 29.1% below its February 2026 peak and down 16.19% over the past year, trailing the Nifty
Large ongoing capex (₹32,700 crore FY27 target, ₹1.3 lakh crore of borrowings) tied to refinery expansion execution and funding
analysis.one_thing: Whether the elevated refining margin and government LPG compensation seen in Q2 FY27 persist into Q3 FY27 (results expected late January/early February 2027) once the one-off subsidy booking is gone - that will show whether this quarter's profit was a turnaround or a one-time spike.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 PAT figures were cross-checked across Business Standard, PSU Connect and IncredMoney and are consistent (standalone ₹21,630 crore, consolidated ₹22,503 crore). P/E and debt/equity figures vary by source - P/E ranges 4.02x to 6.45x across screener-type sites; an initial debt/equity figure of ~9.6x derived from one source used share capital rather than net worth and was set aside in favor of the cross-checked ~0.6x. The Q1 FY27 loss figure differs between standalone (~-₹2,661 crore, most widely reported) and consolidated (-₹1,141 crore, per one screener source) - both are cited above rather than averaged. Promoter pledge data could not be verified from available sources.
